section_summary.extract_value: This section presents a general discussion of a study introducing the CEMS (Caregiver Eating Messages Scale), which measures individuals' perceptions of their caregivers' restrictive/critical eating messages and pressure to eat. The CEMS was developed with expert evaluation from multiple disciplines and demonstrated a two-factor structure with internally consistent and stable scores over a 4-week period. The accompanying figure (Fig. 3) displays a path model testing negative body attitudes and maladaptive eating, showing relationships between BMI, restrictive/critical messages, family pressures, body dissatisfaction, and eating disorder symptomatology, with separate path coefficients reported for women (above paths) and men (below paths).
section_summary.evidence_source: Text content provided and Figure 3 caption and diagram.

Asset Caption.extract_value: Fig. 3. Test of the negative body attitudes and maladaptive eating model. Total scale and subscale scores serve as observed variables in the model. RCM = Restrictive Critical Messages subscale of the Caregiver Eating Messages Scale, PSPS-Family = Family subscale of the Perceived Sociocultural Pressures Scale, EDI-BD = Body Dissatisfaction subscale of the Eating Disorder Inventory-2, and EAT-26 = Eating Attitudes Test-26. Path coefficients above the path are for women; path coefficients below the path are for men. * p < .05.
